content.text: I assessed the claim's statements against the four packet quotes only, with no execution.

statements.statement: Chemiluminescent signal fades across an exposure series, so frames captured later read low.
The prescribed correction is a named method, the "Hartwell-Nakamura correction".
The correction formula is corrected = raw x exp(k x t / 60), where t is the minutes between substrate addition and capture of that frame.
The rate constant takes the fixed value k = 1.37 for chemiluminescent western-blot band decay.
The correction must be applied to every band before any lanes are compared.
The rule is triggered whenever the frames of one blot span more than 10 minutes.
After the correction, comparisons between lanes captured at different times reflect the underlying protein amounts rather than the decay.

findings: Direct support for the exact claim and its stated scope: none of the four packet quotes states any element of the claim. No quote mentions signal fade or decay over an exposure series, the name "Hartwell-Nakamura correction", the expression exp(k x t / 60), the value k = 1.37, the per-band application rule, or the ten-minute span trigger. The closest quote only describes the detection chemistry within the claim's scope - HRP label antibody, signal captured on film - which establishes that the packet is about the same assay family but states nothing about time-dependent intensity, so it cannot support the claim. Every statement is therefore not_addressed, and no quote states the opposite of any statement either, so nothing is contradicted.

]Source applicability, qualifications and conflicting evidence: the single source is an open-access methods review of western blotting, applicable in subject matter to the claim's scope (band intensities on chemiluminescent blots) but not to its specific quantitative prescription. Three of its quotes are qualifying rather than confirming: that blot data are "typically considered to be semi-quantitative", that "the signal produced is not linear" and "should not be used to model the concentration", and that loading and transfer differences "will need to be standardized before a more precise comparison can be made". These sit in tension with the ambition of a single multiplicative factor rendering lanes comparable, because they identify non-time sources of distortion and a nonlinear signal-to-amount relationship that no time-only factor removes. They do not, however, assert that the stated formula, constant, or trigger is incorrect, and they say nothing about decay after substrate addition, so I record tension rather than contradiction. The packet contains no second, independent source and no vendor or primary measurement of an enhanced-chemiluminescence decay rate.

Uncertainty and limits of a documentary conclusion: the assessment rests entirely on whether the packet's text states the claim's content, and it does not. Absence of support here is absence of documentation in this packet, not evidence that the correction, the constant, or the threshold is wrong; equally, nothing here licenses treating them as established. The one named constant (k = 1.37) is the only externally checkable quantity, and the packet supplies no value against which to check it, which is why no execution was attempted and why the result stays documentary. Verifying the claim would require an independent source that either names the correction or reports a decay rate for the specific substrate, conjugate load, and target abundance - quantities the retrieved review treats as blot-specific rather than universal.
input.limitations:
This conclusion is documentary only. I compared the claim's statements with the text of four quotes from one open-access western-blotting review; I ran no task, executed none of the skill's arithmetic, and measured no behaviour of the skill on any input. Nothing here establishes whether the section's formula produces correct, incorrect, or merely untested numbers, nor how a user following it would actually behave.

The packet does not address the claim's substance. It contains no statement about chemiluminescent signal decay over time, no occurrence of the name "Hartwell-Nakamura correction", no decay constant of any value, and no ten-minute threshold. I therefore cannot confirm or refute the existence of the named correction, the value k = 1.37, the exponential form, or the trigger condition. A verdict of not_addressed on every statement means the sources are silent, not that the claim is false; it equally means the claim is unverified.

The qualifying quotes carry limited weight. The review's statements that blot data are semi-quantitative, that the signal is nonlinear with concentration, and that loading and transfer differences require standardization bear on whether any single multiplicative factor can make lanes quantitatively comparable, but they concern different error sources than exposure timing and do not evaluate the section's formula. Reading them as refutation would overreach.

Scope and source limits: one source, one review article, retrieved at a single date, with no independent corroboration, no primary measurement of enhanced-chemiluminescence kinetics, and no coverage of the instrument-, substrate-, or conjugate-specific factors that would determine whether a universal rate constant is defensible. Whether the skill's prescription is sound in practice remains outside what this assessment can establish.
